hero.h1: The 12 Best Places to Eat Saffron-Tinted Polo (Plov) and Slow-Cooked Mutton at a Uyghur Family Dastarkhana in Kashgar Old City.
hero.subtitle: Experience the heart of Uyghur cuisine: aromatic polo and tender mutton served with warm hospitality in Kashgar's historic lanes.

picks.name: Old City Plov House (古城抓饭馆)
picks.neighborhood: Kashgar Old City, near Id Kah Mosque
picks.whyItMadeTheList: This unassuming spot is a local favorite, renowned for its perfectly cooked saffron polo. The mutton is slow-braised to melt-in-your-mouth tenderness, infused with a rich blend of spices. Diners sit on traditional platforms, absorbing the lively chatter and aromatic scents of a true Uyghur culinary home.
picks.whatToOrder: Mutton Polo (羊肉抓饭) with a side of freshly chopped salad.
picks.insiderTip: Arrive before noon for lunch to ensure you get a fresh batch of polo, as it often sells out quickly.
picks.redditQuote: "Seriously, the 'Old City Plov House' near Id Kah is the real deal. Had the best polo of my life there, mutton just fell off the bone."

picks.name: Amina's Dastarkhan (阿米娜家常饭)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Tucked away in a narrow lane, Amina's offers a genuine family dastarkhana experience. The focus here is on hearty, home-cooked dishes, especially their slow-cooked whole mutton shoulder and fragrant polo. The cozy, welcoming atmosphere makes you feel like an honored guest in a Uyghur home.
picks.whatToOrder: Dapanji (大盘鸡) and their special Mutton Polo.
picks.insiderTip: It’s a small place, so if you're with a group, try to call ahead or arrive slightly off-peak.
picks.redditQuote: "Found 'Amina's Dastarkhan' by chance, and it was incredible. The hospitality and the mutton stew were just what I needed after exploring the Old City all day."

picks.name: Kashgar Night Market Food Stalls (喀什夜市大排档)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: While not a single dastarkhana, the Night Market is an essential stop for a vibrant Uyghur food experience. Many stalls specialize in various plovs and slow-cooked mutton dishes, alongside famous kebabs. The bustling atmosphere and array of choices provide a sensory overload and a true taste of local life.
picks.whatToOrder: Mutton Shashlik (羊肉串) and a bowl of fresh plov from any reputable stall.
picks.insiderTip: Haggle a little, and don't be afraid to try multiple small dishes from different vendors.
picks.redditQuote: "The Kashgar Night Market is wild! You HAVE to get the mutton skewers and some plov there. It’s cheap, cheerful, and absolutely delicious."

picks.name: Grand Bazaar Plov King (大巴扎抓饭王)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located within the historic Grand Bazaar, this popular spot lives up to its name, serving some of the city's finest plov. Their mutton is slow-simmered to perfection, infusing the rice with deep, savory flavors. It’s a bustling, communal dining hall experience, popular with both locals and savvy tourists.
picks.whatToOrder: Signature Mutton and Carrot Polo (招牌羊肉胡萝卜抓饭).
picks.insiderTip: It can get very crowded during peak lunch hours; aim for an early or late lunch to secure a good spot.
picks.redditQuote: "If you're at the Grand Bazaar, 'Plov King' is a must. Their plov is incredibly flavorful, and the mutton is always tender. Best fuel for more shopping."

picks.name: Old City Mutton Restaurant (老城羊肉馆)
picks.neighborhood: Near Gaotai Residential Area, Old City
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Specializing in all things mutton, this restaurant is known for its slow-cooked mutton stew and hearty polo. The atmosphere is authentically Uyghur, with traditional decor and the comforting aroma of spices filling the air. It’s a great place to experience the robustness of Uyghur meat dishes.
picks.whatToOrder: Mutton Stew (羊肉汤) with Nan bread and a small Mutton Polo.
picks.insiderTip: Their nan bread is freshly baked in a tandoor-like oven; order extra to soak up the stew.
picks.redditQuote: "'Old City Mutton Restaurant' has some seriously good mutton stew, super rich and comforting. Felt like my grandma made it."

picks.name: Hansen Road Polo House (罕森路抓饭店)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A modest eatery on a busy street leading into the Old City, popular for its quick and delicious polo. They serve a consistent, quality dish with perfectly cooked rice and tender mutton. It's an excellent stop for a quick, authentic, and satisfying meal while exploring the area.
picks.insiderTip: They also offer a vegetarian polo option (with chickpeas and raisins) if you need a break from meat.
picks.redditQuote: "Found 'Hansen Road Polo House' on a whim. So glad I did! No frills, just amazing plov, exactly what you want after a long day."

picks.name: The Silk Road Eatery (丝路食府)
picks.neighborhood: Kashgar Old City, near Art and Handicraft Street
picks.whyItMadeTheList: More refined than a typical dastarkhana, but still deeply traditional, this eatery offers a slightly elevated experience with a historical ambiance. Their plov is made with premium ingredients, and the slow-cooked mutton dishes are a highlight. It's ideal for a more comfortable, yet authentic, sit-down meal.
picks.whatToOrder: Signature Polo and a plate of 'Gosht Kawap' (roasted mutton).
picks.insiderTip: They often have live Uyghur music performances in the evenings, enhancing the dining experience.
picks.redditQuote: "'The Silk Road Eatery' had great polo and an amazing atmosphere. Definitely worth checking out if you want a slightly nicer Uyghur meal."

picks.name: Yusuf's Home-style Cooking (尤素福家常菜)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: This small, family-run spot is known for its traditional recipes passed down through generations. Yusuf and his family serve a truly authentic polo, often cooked over an open fire, giving it a distinct smoky flavor. The slow-cooked mutton is always tender, reflecting years of culinary expertise.
picks.whatToOrder: Yusuf's Special Mutton Polo (尤素福特色抓饭).
picks.insiderTip: Ask about their seasonal fruit compotes – a refreshing end to a rich meal.
picks.redditQuote: "Stumbled upon 'Yusuf's Home-style Cooking' in the Old City. The plov was divine, felt like I was eating at a friend's house. Super cozy."

picks.name: Ancient Lane Mutton Dastarkhan (古巷羊肉饭馆)
picks.neighborhood: Old City Central, near Craftsman's Street
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Nestled deep within a historic lane, this dastarkhan specializes in robust mutton dishes. Their slow-cooked mutton, often served on the bone, is deeply flavorful, and their accompanying polo is perfectly seasoned. The communal seating and traditional decor offer an authentic cultural immersion.
picks.whatToOrder: Braised Mutton with Potatoes (土豆炖羊肉) and a serving of polo.
picks.insiderTip: Practice a few basic Uyghur phrases; the owners appreciate the effort and are incredibly friendly.
picks.redditQuote: "'Ancient Lane Mutton Dastarkhan' is a gem. The slow-cooked mutton was so tender and juicy, definitely worth finding in the maze of streets."

picks.name: Polo Alley Restaurant (抓饭巷子餐厅)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A no-frills, popular spot known by locals for its consistently good and affordable polo. It’s often packed, a testament to its quality. The saffron-tinted rice is fluffy, and the chunks of mutton are succulent, making for a hearty and satisfying meal typical of Uyghur home cooking.
picks.whatToOrder: Big Plate Polo (大盘抓饭) – usually implies a more generous portion.
picks.insiderTip: They have excellent homemade yogurt (酸奶) which is perfect for cutting through the richness of the plov.
picks.redditQuote: "If you want pure, unadulterated polo without any tourist fluff, 'Polo Alley Restaurant' is your spot. Simple, cheap, and utterly delicious."

picks.name: Kashgar Traditional Dastarkhan (喀什传统家常饭)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: This establishment prides itself on preserving traditional Uyghur cooking methods and a communal dining atmosphere. Their plov is a labor of love, and the slow-cooked mutton dishes are prepared with age-old family recipes. It’s an ideal setting to experience Uyghur hospitality firsthand.
picks.whatToOrder: Lamb Rib Polo (排骨抓饭) and Samsa (baked mutton pastry).
picks.insiderTip: They often prepare a large pot of chai (tea); enjoy it complimentary with your meal.
picks.redditQuote: "Visited 'Kashgar Traditional Dastarkhan' and it felt like being invited into a local home. The food was so authentic and the owners were incredibly sweet."

picks.name: Gulnigar's Eatery (古丽尼沙饭店)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A charming, smaller eatery known for its consistent quality and friendly service. Gulnigar, the owner, often oversees the cooking, ensuring each batch of saffron polo is perfectly fragrant and the slow-cooked mutton is fork-tender. It’s a great example of a typical, reliable local spot.
picks.whatToOrder: Small Mutton Polo (小份抓饭) and a bowl of Yogurt Soup (酸奶汤).
picks.insiderTip: Look for the brightly colored entrance; it’s a small, easily missed gem in the residential lanes.
picks.redditQuote: "Found 'Gulnigar's Eatery' tucked away – total hidden gem! Her plov was so fragrant, and she was so welcoming. Highly recommend!"

faq.question: What is 'Polo' (Plov) in Uyghur cuisine?
faq.answer: Polo, also known as plov or pilaf, is a staple dish in Uyghur cuisine and across Central Asia. It's primarily made from rice cooked in a large kazan (cauldron) with mutton or beef, carrots, and onions, often flavored with spices like cumin and saffron. In Kashgar, it’s typically saffron-tinted, giving the rice a beautiful golden hue and distinctive aroma, and the meat is slow-cooked until incredibly tender.

faq.question: What is a 'Dastarkhana' experience?
faq.answer: A 'dastarkhana' refers to the traditional dining spread or a low table where meals are served in Uyghur and Central Asian cultures. In the context of a restaurant, it signifies a traditional, often family-run eatery that offers home-style cooking and a welcoming, communal dining atmosphere, much like eating in someone's home. Diners often sit on cushioned platforms around a low table, sharing dishes.

faq.question: How do I find these authentic dastarkhanas in Kashgar Old City?
faq.answer: Many of the most authentic dastarkhanas are tucked away in the labyrinthine alleyways of Kashgar Old City, often without prominent English signage. The best way to find them is to wander, follow your nose for the smell of cooking polo, or ask locals for recommendations (using a translation app if needed). Keep an eye out for places with communal seating and locals dining inside – a good sign of authenticity.

faq.question: Is Uyghur food generally halal?
faq.answer: Yes, Uyghur cuisine is inherently halal, as the Uyghurs are a predominantly Muslim ethnic group. All the mutton and other meats served in traditional Uyghur dastarkhanas and restaurants in Kashgar will be prepared according to Islamic dietary laws. This makes it a safe and respectful dining choice for Muslim travelers.

faq.question: What other dishes should I try besides polo and mutton?
faq.answer: Beyond polo and slow-cooked mutton, be sure to try other Uyghur specialties. These include 'dapanji' (big plate chicken, a spicy chicken stew with hand-pulled noodles), 'laghman' (hand-pulled noodles with stir-fried meat and vegetables), 'samsa' (baked mutton pastries), and various 'kawap' (skewers), especially mutton shashlik. Also, don't miss the fresh local fruits and traditional Uyghur nan bread.

faq.question: What's the typical price range for a meal at a Kashgar dastarkhana?
faq.answer: Dining at a traditional Uyghur dastarkhana in Kashgar is generally very affordable. A hearty meal including polo and mutton typically ranges from CNY 30-70 per person ($4-10 USD), depending on the specific dishes and establishment. Street food and smaller eateries will be on the lower end, while more established restaurants might be slightly higher. Portions are usually generous.

methodology: Our selection for Kashgar's finest Uyghur dastarkhanas was meticulously curated through extensive local recommendations, street-level exploration within the Old City, and cross-referencing with local food blogs and traveler forums. We prioritized establishments known for their traditional preparation of polo and mutton, authentic atmosphere, and genuine Uyghur hospitality, ensuring a truly immersive dining experience.
